Numa Triples ARR, Raises $45M Series C to Run the Entire Dealership
News provided by
Numa
Nov 16, 2026, 10:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Led by Blue Cloud Ventures, the round brings total funding to $96 million, with more than 1,500 dealerships across the U.S. and Canada already running on Numa's AI Operating System
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Numa , the AI Operating System for dealerships, today announced a $45 million Series C led by Blue Cloud Ventures, with participation from Threshold Ventures, Costanoa, Touring Capital, Gradient Ventures and Tokio Marine Future Fund. The round brings Numa's total funding to $96 million. It caps a year in which Numa tripled in size, tripled its annual recurring revenue and became the AI system GM, FordDirect, BMW and Stellantis each put in front of their dealerships.
Numa has already won the hardest part of the dealership: the customer conversation. The system has handled more than 1 billion calls, texts and chats and booked more than 4 million appointments. Dealerships that run on Numa stay and grow with it. Net revenue retention has risen over the past year, and more dealerships are moving to longer agreements.
For decades, dealership software was built one task at a time. Each system kept its own record of what happened, and none of them acted on what the customer just said. The first wave of AI did not change that. It answered faster, then handed the work back to people to chase by hand.
Numa does not hand the work back. It knows not just who the customer is but what they need, and it acts on it: booking the visit, finding the right car, routing the call or flagging the customer about to leave.
"In two years, every general manager will have an AI COO," said Tasso Roumeliotis, founder and CEO of Numa. "At more than 1,500 dealerships, they already do, and it is Numa. It knows every conversation in the store, sees what needs attention and runs the work that follows. That is not another dashboard or another point tool. It is an operating system. The DMS was built to record the dealership. It was never built to run it. Numa was, and this round puts more engineers to accelerate it."
"What is unique about Numa is that the company understands the DNA and culture of a dealership and seamlessly AI-enables the workflow while empowering all constituents including the dealerships customers", added Mir Arif, Managing Partner of Blue Cloud Ventures. "Numa is not prescriptive but rather deeply understands the objectives of the BDC representative, the salesperson, the service technician, the parts specialist and the sales manager and significantly enhances their productivity."
"As an insurer, we view dealerships as a critical part of the ecosystem that supports customers throughout their vehicle ownership journey," said Mitsutoshi Shizuru, Managing Executive Officer of Tokio Marine & Nichido Fire Insurance Co., Ltd, "Numa is using AI to make this important customer touchpoint faster, more efficient, and more seamless. We believe Numa's technology has the potential to revolutionize the relationship between dealerships and their customers and help shape the next generation of mobility customer experiences in the U.S. and beyond."
This year, Numa took its system across the whole store.

Mount Thor, a start-up specialising in Apple-based computing infrastructure, has raised US$45 million through two funding rounds as it looks to expand its data centre services for artificial intelligence (AI) agents.
The company operates racks of Apple computers that provide remote access to macOS environments for businesses, developers and AI research teams. Its approach addresses the growing need for computing infrastructure that can run tasks that depend on Apple’s operating system and applications.
As AI agents become more capable of performing tasks through computer interfaces, access to traditional cloud infrastructure may not always be sufficient. Some applications and workflows require macOS-specific features, creating demand for dedicated Mac environments that can be accessed remotely.
Mount Thor aims to meet this demand by providing businesses with managed access to Mac hardware without requiring them to purchase, maintain and operate large fleets of Apple computers themselves. The funding will support the company’s infrastructure expansion, recruitment and research into running AI models on Apple silicon.
Mount Thor targets the growing demand for Mac-based AI infrastructure
AI agents are increasingly being developed to interact with computers like human users. Rather than simply responding to written instructions, these systems can navigate software, manage files, operate applications and complete tasks through graphical interfaces.
Some agents are designed to work independently for extended periods, while others respond to requests as they arrive. These capabilities create new infrastructure requirements, particularly when agents need access to desktop environments to perform their assigned work.
However, conventional cloud computing systems do not always provide the software compatibility these operations require. Applications designed specifically for macOS, along with features available through Apple’s ecosystem, can make Mac hardware necessary for certain development and deployment tasks.
Mount Thor provides remotely accessible Mac systems that let organisations create and run these environments without managing the physical equipment. The service targets research laboratories, software developers, and companies building AI-powered platforms.

Businesses developing autonomous agent platforms could also use Mount Thor’s machines to provide individual macOS workspaces. These environments could remain active for weeks, allowing agents to keep working on tasks without a human physically operating a computer.

articles.title: Southland Holdings: $34 Million Tunnel Project And New Data Center Contracts Awarded
articles.snippet:
Southland Holdings has secured a $34 million tunnel construction project in the Southwest along with additional contracts supporting data center construction in the Mid-Atlantic and Southwest. The awards expand activity across the company's civil infrastructure business as demand continues for specialized construction services supporting transportation and digital infrastructure.
The post Southland Holdings: $34 Million Tunnel Project And New Data Center Contracts Awarded appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Southland Holdings: $34 Million Tunnel Project And New Data Center Contracts Awarded
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 8:55 PM
Southland Holdings: $34 Million Tunnel Project And New Data Center Contracts Awarded
Southland Holdings has secured a $34 million tunnel construction project in the Southwest along with additional contracts supporting data center construction in the Mid-Atlantic and Southwest. The awards expand activity across the company’s civil infrastructure business as demand continues for specialized construction services supporting transportation and digital infrastructure.
Two Southland subsidiaries within its Civil segment will perform the newly awarded work.
Southland Contracting received the $34 million tunnel project, which includes the design and installation of approximately 5,800 linear feet of liner-plate crossings.
The project scope also includes associated shafts, shoring, and grouting work.
The award adds to Southland’s tunnel construction operations, which form part of its broader infrastructure services business.
Separately, Oscar Renda Contracting secured a master service agreement to provide labor and equipment at a data center site in the Mid-Atlantic.
The subsidiary also received two contracts, including another master service agreement, for work at a data center location in the Southwest.
The data center agreements will provide construction-related labor and equipment services as directed by the customer.
Southland has not disclosed a final contract value for the data center work. The amount will depend on the actual quantities of services and equipment required during project execution.
The company also clarified that the data center agreements are project-specific and are not recurring contracts.
The awards provide Southland with additional exposure to the data center construction market, where infrastructure development requires specialized construction capabilities and supporting services.
Data centers depend on extensive physical infrastructure, including power systems, cooling equipment, utility connections, and supporting facilities. Construction activity in the sector creates opportunities for contractors involved in site preparation, civil engineering, and related infrastructure work.
Southland operates across several infrastructure markets, including bridges, tunneling, transportation, communications, marine construction, steel structures, water and wastewater treatment, and water pipelines.
Its subsidiaries provide specialized construction services for public and private sector projects throughout North America and internationally.
The company traces its roots to 1900 and is headquartered in Grapevine, Texas.
The latest awards reinforce the company’s participation in two infrastructure markets receiving substantial investment: underground transportation and utility infrastructure, and data center development.
The $34 million tunnel project provides a defined contract value, while the additional data center agreements create opportunities for further project revenue based on customer-directed work.
Southland did not provide project completion schedules or anticipated revenue recognition timelines for the new awards.

The University of Tennessee has secured up to $27 million in renewed sponsorship from the U.S. Department of War's Army Research Laboratory to advance materials science and manufacturing technologies supporting military applications.
The post University Of Tennessee: $27 Million Army Research Laboratory Renewal To Advance Military Materials And Manufacturing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
University Of Tennessee: $27 Million Army Research Laboratory Renewal To Advance Military Materials And Manufacturing
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 5:34 PM
University Of Tennessee: $27 Million Army Research Laboratory Renewal To Advance Military Materials And Manufacturing
The University of Tennessee has secured up to $27 million in renewed sponsorship from the U.S. Department of War’s Army Research Laboratory to advance materials science and manufacturing technologies supporting military applications.
The funding will support the university’s multidisciplinary Defense Development and Applied Research Center (DARC) and multiple departments within the Tickle College of Engineering from 2026 through 2030.
The research focuses on developing advanced materials, improving manufacturing processes, and addressing supply chain challenges affecting military equipment.
New Partnership With Leidos
The renewed sponsorship will support a new research partnership between the university and industrial partner Leidos.
The collaboration will examine equipment assembly timelines and identify supply chain bottlenecks that could be addressed through additive manufacturing.
Researchers will investigate alternative manufacturing approaches that can produce mission-critical components faster or at lower cost while maintaining or improving performance.
The university’s capabilities include developing carbon-based composites, hybrid materials, and ceramic composites designed to withstand demanding operating environments.
Researchers also use advanced imaging and characterization equipment to evaluate complex materials, including additively manufactured components.
Expanding Research Collaboration Across Tennessee
The funding will also expand collaboration with the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga.
Starting in 2026, researchers at UTC’s Nanoengineering Center will contribute theoretical and simulation expertise to complement UT Knoxville’s experimental materials research.
High-fidelity simulations will help researchers understand the mechanisms responsible for material performance and degradation.
AI-assisted predictive models will also help reduce reliance on trial-and-error experimentation.
The collaboration is intended to generate more information from each experiment while accelerating the development of materials for military applications.
Developing Materials For Extreme Environments
Military equipment frequently operates under extreme temperatures, mechanical stresses, and other challenging conditions.
The university is developing lightweight, stable, and fatigue-tolerant composites that combine the strengths of multiple materials.
These technologies could improve the performance and reliability of military components while supporting more efficient manufacturing.
The renewed ARL sponsorship also provides research opportunities for faculty and students across the university system.
KEY QUOTES:
“As fundamental scientists, we’re trying to understand a material’s chemistry, structure, and performance—but integrating with ARL means we’re also hearing from the folks who will eventually deploy it. That accelerates the translation of new technologies into deployable solutions.”
Katharine Page, Professor Of Materials Science And Engineering And Lead Investigator For DARC’s ARL Research
“By combining experiments and modeling, we can learn more from each experiment and use that knowledge to guide material development.”
Murat Barisik, Director Of The Nanoengin
